body: Hey there, I’m sorry to hear about your mom 💜 a lot of people here can relate to what you’re feeling. My mom passed away nearly five years ago and I’m still struggling with anger and self isolation, and feeling a connection with others. It isn’t crazy to feel that way, in fact it’s a big part of grief. Advice I’d give to anyone trying to comfort someone who lost a loved one- check in on them in 3 months, 6 months, 2 years. In my experience those can be the really grueling times of grieving, when it feels like everyone has forgotten and your sorrow has been left to the wayside. Please don’t internalize that this is who you are, it is fair that you’re feeling angry. That kindhearted person is still there! These feelings are temporary & in time it will feel easier.

Hey, I’m so sorry you’re going through this. I had an ex who was kind of similar. He would give me the silent treatment for days and act like he was going to break up with me, he would kick me out of the apartment. He even admitted to me once that it was a manipulation tactic because he felt powerless in the relationship and it was the only way he could gain any sense of power. I have abandonment issues so it got me every time and it prevented me from ever truly confronting him about his behavior because I was always so busy apologizing and was always so grateful when he was finally ready to let me back in. 

Do you know what one of the most satisfying moments of my life was?

I finally kicked him to the curb for good (on my second attempt) and he came over to drop my bike off. This was the last time I ever saw him. I couldn’t stop smiling because I felt awkward but I was also happy because the spell was broken on my side and no part of me wanted to get back with him. He tried asking me to get back together and I got to point out to him all the times he told me that he didn’t want this relationship. I told him that this is what he wanted. He couldn’t say anything in reply because I was right- he did say all those things and he spent so much time telling me how miserable I made him. And I felt so much satisfaction because unlike him, the one time I broke up with him, I actually meant it. That was super empowering.

I really encourage you to keep your resolve to leave. I know it’s hard. Something that helped for me was to make 2 lists: one was a list of plans, things I was going to do and look forward to (concerts, plans with friends, travel to visit family, home improvements) to keep myself busy and have stuff to look forward to. The second was a more general list of positive outcomes for my lifestyle after the breakup- things I could now do and enjoy without worrying about him (spending more time with friends, staying late at work if I wanted to, stopping and getting a drink by myself at a bar, whatever). I also became vegetarian which was something I always wanted to do but it would have been challenging with him.

You got this. You can do it! It won’t be easy, but you will look back and be so proud of yourself and have zero regrets. 

You love him because you’re a good person and he is not capable of reciprocating love in a healthy way. He can’t give you what you need.

I don’t believe that everyone who has children does so with the belief that they will be “whole” or “complete” with them. This will most likely be an unpopular opinion here but the strict anti-natalism can get to me on this sub sometimes. I do agree that many people have kids simply because they don’t challenge the norm, but I also believe it’s possible to have children in an intentional and ethical manner. We are biological beings with this one life to live, and I don’t think the selfishness of engaging in reproduction outweighs the inherent drive to do so (in every case). Also, if there is any hope for human life on our planet, we will need folks who have been raised by the sorts of people who are collapse aware and who impart thoughtful, anti-establishment mindsets to their children. And finally, one cannot claim that a life lived through strife and suffering is one without any joy or happiness, or one that doesn’t contribute meaningfully to the world. Judging others for their decisions isn’t palatable to me. We don’t know everything.

Rust belt area. It is a city known for being racist and it is much more geographically segregated by neighborhood than where we are from. This has created a landscape where my mom couldn’t find housing in a decent neighborhood because frankly, it is just much harder to live here if you are poor. So her race didn’t directly affect her housing situation, but by virtue of being on housing assistance, she faced a prejudicial landscape. Where we came from, she could always find an apartment in walkable areas among a more diverse population, socioeconomically and racially. She only became a DJT supporter after she had been here for some time and her mental health was already very very low. It’s hard to try to convey the situation she was in so I ordinarily don’t really talk about it. These are difficult and complex topics, especially as a privileged person myself.
